issues.description: Negative-seed grammar accepts a stray sign on the increment too
issues.detail: IdentityGrammar now allows SignedSegmentGrammar before both numeric literals. That's fine for seed, but increment normally isn't written with a leading +/- in practice; the grammar would now happily parse IDENTITY(1, -1) and IDENTITY(+1, +1). Probably harmless and arguably correct (TSQL does allow negative increment), but worth a one-line comment in the grammar so future readers know the symmetry is intentional rather than copy-paste.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE numeric form has no test fixture
issues.detail: The grammar for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE was widened to accept NumericLiteralSegment, QuotedLiteralSegment, or NakedIdentifierSegment. The added create_login.sql fixture only exercises the naked-identifier form (us_english). If the numeric LCID form is worth supporting in the parser, it's worth one line in the fixture to lock it down; otherwise drop NumericLiteralSegment and keep the grammar smaller. Pick one.

issues.description: DROP COLUMN / DROP CONSTRAINT branches duplicate structure that could share a small helper
issues.detail: The two new DROP branches are near-identical in shape: outer Sequence("DROP", Delimited(Sequence(<keyword>, Ref("IfExistsGrammar", optional=True), <reference>))). Inlining both is fine and arguably the Pike-approved move (n is 2; a helper would be cleverness for cleverness's sake). Leaving this as a P2 note rather than a fix: if a third DROP-ish variant shows up, factor then, not now.

issues.description: Removed alter_table fixture loses real coverage of mixed ADD/DROP in one statement
issues.detail: The deleted fixture combined ADD column-with-constraint and two DROP COLUMNs in a single ALTER TABLE, comma-delimited. The PR removes it because the outer Delimited around the whole OneOf is gone (you can no longer mix an ADD and a DROP in one ALTER TABLE in this grammar). That matches the MS docs for most cases, but the old example was directly from the Microsoft sp_help doc page. Worth confirming this is intentional scope reduction (TSQL does allow some mixed forms) rather than accidental regression; if intentional, a one-line comment near the grammar would save the next maintainer a git-blame trip.

review.summary: The change is mostly mechanical TSQL grammar widening: table-variable indexes, CREATE LOGIN with naked identifiers and N'...' passwords, negative IDENTITY seeds, and a restructured ALTER TABLE that moves Delimited inward so DROP COLUMN and DROP CONSTRAINT can each take a list. The data shape (grammar tree) is the right thing to fix here, not the algorithm — SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE in spirit. The one structural concern: the outer Delimited around ALTER TABLE's OneOf was removed, which drops support for mixing ADD and DROP in one statement; the test fixture that exercised that case was deleted alongside it. Verify that's intentional scope-reduction rather than a regression. Otherwise the diff is tidy, the YAML hashes look right, and the new fixtures cover the new branches adequately.
